records.title: Epigenetics in inflammatory bowel disease: from mechanistic insights to personalized therapeutic strategies
records.description: This Review discusses the complex role of epigenetics in inflammatory bowel disease and provides a comprehensive overview of current and emerging technologies that could enhance the prognostic value of epigenetic biomarkers.

records.title: PDE4 inhibition at the crossroads of IBD and obesity
records.description: Obesity and inflammatory bowel disease are increasingly recognized as interconnected inflammatory and metabolic disorders. New insights into glucagon-like peptide-1 signalling highlight the role of phosphodiesterase 4 in energy balance. Although phosphodiesterase 4 inhibitors have previously been studied in inflammatory bowel disease, their potential to address both gut inflammation and obesity remains unexplored.

records.title: Choosing the right drug for the right patient with steatohepatitis
records.description: With resmetirom and semaglutide approved for non-cirrhotic steatohepatitis with fibrosis, new European guidance moves the question from whether to treat to whom to treat, and with what. The noninvasive, phenotype-driven framework of these guidelines will shape clinical practice, yet much of the recommendations rests on expert consensus rather than comparative or outcome data.

records.title: Cholestasis of unknown origin in adults: more than genes
records.description: Despite advances in hepatology and genetics, chronic cholestasis in adults often remains unexplained. The ‘cholestatic exposome’ provides an integrative framework linking cumulative environmental exposures with inherited susceptibility of liver epithelial cells, potentially explaining incomplete penetrance, disease onset, progression and clinical phenotype heterogeneity beyond the limitations of a purely gene-centred model.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Conceptual framework and expert guidance on intrapancreatic fat deposition: the Melbourne consensus
Timing matters in hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation
Oral IL-23 receptor blockade shows promise in ulcerative colitis
The genomic and epigenomic evolution of colorectal cancer
records.description: This Review describes the genomic and epigenomic evolution of colorectal cancer, and the implications of evolutionary mechanisms for treatment strategies and patient management.

records.title: Gut fungi linked to development of MASLD-HCC
Limited efficacy of faecal microbiota transplantation in IBS
Baveno VIII refines the continuum of advanced chronic liver disease and portal hypertension
records.description: The Baveno VIII consensus, published in 2026, builds on the framework established by Baveno VII, adding new recommendations that refine the management of advanced chronic parenchymal and vascular liver diseases and further establish portal hypertension as a continuum across disease stages.

records.title: Laying the foundations for clinical microbiome research
records.description: Microbiome science is moving on from discovery to implementation, but implementation requires standards to ensure that clinical microbiome research can truly move from bench to bedside.

records.title: Training the next generation of hepatologists for the cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic era
records.description: As metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease changes the clinical profile and care needs of patients with liver disease, hepatology training must extend beyond traditional organ-based boundaries. Hepatologists will increasingly need skills in cardiovascular, kidney and metabolic risk assessment, treatment co-management and referral, alongside their core expertise in liver disease.

records.title: Primary cilia: sensors of biliary homeostasis and disease
records.description: Primary cilia, organelles found in cholangiocytes, regulate biliary homeostasis and regeneration. This Review discusses how alterations in primary-cilium structure and function can lead to biliary ciliopathies and provides a detailed overview of the underlying mechanisms.

records.title: Perioperative immunotherapy for resectable gastric and gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma: overall survival results
Antifungal therapy reshapes the gut microbiota in IBD
CHESS-LiverHealth: community prevalence of chronic liver disease in China
Building the next generation of gastroenterology and hepatology research leaders in Asia: from disease burden to scientific leadership
records.description: Asia bears a disproportionate burden of digestive and liver diseases but remains under-represented in global research leadership. This Comment examines structural, cultural and institutional barriers to developing clinician-scientists in Asia, highlights successful regional models and proposes strategies to strengthen training, mentorship and research capacity.

records.title: ESPEN 2026
The exposome and inflammatory bowel disease: a framework for primary and primordial prevention
records.description: The environment is a critical factor in the development of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). In this Perspective, the authors summarize the latest evidence on the exposome and IBD risk, encompassing physical, chemical, biological and psychosocial components. They discuss innovation and challenges alongside a framework for IBD prevention by modulating the exposome.

records.title: Drug–microbiome–host interactions: antimicrobial effects of non-antibiotic compounds
records.description: Many compounds not classified as antibiotics can exert antimicrobial activity, with drug–microbiome–host interactions having profound effects on the human microbiome and human health. This Review explores how non-antibiotic compounds exert these antimicrobial effects, highlighting which compounds can influence the microbiome, the underlying mechanisms, and implications for translation and clinical practice.

records.title: Occult hepatitis B virus infection
records.description: In this Review, Yuen and colleagues describe the epidemiology, diagnosis, pathophysiology and clinical management of occult hepatitis B virus infection, and propose some future directions for research.

records.title: Beyond inflammation: the residual burden as the next target in inflammatory bowel disease
records.description: A notable subset of people with inflammatory bowel disease remain unwell despite objective remission. Their ‘residual burden’ is too often misinterpreted as inflammation and can be treated as such. These symptoms, not attributable to active inflammation, deserve to be recognized as a treatment target in their own right and managed alongside disease control.

records.title: Heart–liver co-management in MASLD: expert perspectives and recommendations from a multidisciplinary cardiometabolic framework
records.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is a systemic cardiometabolic disease requiring integrated heart–liver co-management. This Expert Recommendation provides practical guidance on awareness, screening, treatment, clinical trial design and guideline implementation within a multisystem metabolic care framework.

records.title: Building and regenerating intestines by manipulating intestinal stem cells
records.description: Major advances have deepened our understanding of intestinal stem (ISC) biology, yet the clinical translation remains limited, despite the promise of harnessing ISCs for both mucosal repair and regenerating functioning intestinal tissue. This Roadmap outlines progress, challenges and opportunities in the translation of ISC research to clinical therapy.

records.title: Challenges and opportunities in combining radiotherapy and immunotherapy for localized pancreatic cancer
records.description: In this Review, the authors critically discuss the rationale, challenges and opportunities for radiotherapy–immunotherapy combinations in localized pancreatic cancer. Preclinical and clinical data are examined, drawing on evidence from pancreatic cancer and other cancer types and reframing radiation therapy as a potential immunological platform.

records.title: Long non-coding RNAs in colorectal cancer: shaping the tumour microenvironment and advancing precision oncology
records.description: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are emerging as key regulators in cancer progression, including colorectal cancer (CRC). This Review provides a mechanistic overview of the role of lncRNAs in the CRC microenvironment and discusses their potential in precision oncology.

records.title: Closing the policy gap: including children in the global agenda for steatotic liver disease
Reply to ‘Closing the policy gap: including children in the global agenda for steatotic liver disease’
The International Chinese Young Scholars Alliance for the Study of the Liver: facilitating global collaboration
records.description: The global profile of Chinese hepatology has expanded rapidly over the past four decades, driven by major scientific investment, increased global mobility and landmark clinical and translational discoveries. As a new generation of Chinese investigators emerges around the globe, initiatives that foster international collaboration, mentorship and scientific exchange will be essential for advancing the future of global liver research.

records.title: The microbial mirror: how a disrupted microbiome forecasts disease and why policy must act
records.description: Noncommunicable diseases kill 43 million people worldwide yearly, but one of their key biological drivers, the disruption of the gut microbiome by modifiable environmental factors, is still underappreciated by health stakeholders. The translation of microbiome science into concrete actions, from food safety regulators to public health authorities and policymakers, is urgently needed.

records.title: Phase I trial of faecal microbiome transplantation for food allergy
Sexual dimorphism in the liver
records.description: In this Review, Jain and Monga describe the mechanisms of hepatic sexual dimorphism in homeostasis and physiological conditions, as well as in the pathophysiology of diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, autoimmune diseases, viral hepatitis and liver cancer.

records.title: Relieving IBD with duvakitug
Noninvasive testing for fibrosis and cirrhosis in MASLD
From researcher to CEO: closing the gap between discovery and delivery
records.description: A patient advocate asked what decades of fibrosis research meant for the people he represented. I had no answer. That question exposed a gap that the scientific community must now confront: between the knowledge we generate and the means to deliver it to patients.

records.title: Global epidemiology of metabolic and alcohol-associated liver disease: risk factors, natural history and clinical implications
records.description: In this Review, Loomba and colleagues describe the global epidemiology, risk factors, natural history and clinical implications of metabolic and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD).

records.title: Viral pyroptosis linked to lethal hepatic lipid accumulation
Author Correction: The dynamic spectrum of steatotic liver disease: the global perspective
The dynamic spectrum of steatotic liver disease: the global perspective
records.description: Steatotic liver disease encompasses a spectrum of conditions driven by metabolic dysfunction and/or alcohol consumption. This Review provides a comprehensive global overview of the disease and critically examines current therapeutic strategies and future perspectives.

records.title: Multidisciplinary Delphi consensus statement on minimal standards for clinical metadata and end points in microbiome studies
records.description: In this Consensus Statement, an international panel of experts provides recommendations to harmonize metadata, sampling, analysis and end points in gut microbiome-based clinical research.

records.title: Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections
records.description: Anorectal bacterial sexually transmitted infections (STIs) remain a global health challenge. This Review provides an overview of anorectal bacterial STIs focusing on chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis, with insights into global burden, pathophysiology, management and prevention, as well as highlighting knowledge gaps and research priorities.

records.title: Desynchronization of intestinal circadian clocks and gastrointestinal dysfunction
records.description: Intestinal circadian clocks are emerging as important regulators of gastrointestinal physiology and homeostasis. Recent advances suggest that desynchronization of circadian clocks in distinct intestinal cell types could contribute to gastrointestinal dysfunction, highlighting new opportunities to understand disease mechanisms and identify future research priorities.

records.title: Understanding intrapancreatic fat: charting a path forward
records.description: Two independent Delphi-driven consensus initiatives have established the first standardized frameworks for defining, measuring and managing intrapancreatic fat. Their areas of agreement provide a foundation for clinical recognition, while key divergences in terminology, thresholds and evidence appraisal highlight critical questions that must be resolved through rigorous collaborative research.

records.title: Dupilumab shows promise in eosinophilic gastritis
Precision adherence support for hepatitis C treatment
PIEZO1 senses the mechanics of liver regeneration
Steatosis fuels replacement liver metastases in colorectal cancer
Conceptual framework and expert guidance on intrapancreatic fat deposition: the Melbourne consensus
records.description: In this Consensus Statement, a global multidisciplinary group of experts provide a structured framework and clear guidance on intrapancreatic fat deposition and fatty pancreas disorder.

records.title: Features of immune microenvironment associated with colorectal polyp development
Mechanisms and clinical outcomes linking HLA-DRB1*01:03 and IBD
EASL Congress 2026
Advancing liver health in a shifting global landscape
records.description: Global liver health is at a pivotal moment, marked by a rising steatotic liver disease burden alongside stalled progress in viral hepatitis elimination. Strengthening prevention and access to care is essential to reduce inequities, morbidity and mortality worldwide.

records.title: The mesenteric model of abdominal anatomy
records.description: The mesenteric model is a new anatomy of the abdomen that defines a mesentery-based organ system unifying structure, development and function, reveals system-level mechanisms of disease, enables targeted therapies, and provides a coherent scientific foundation for integrating biological research with clinical practice across both abdominal and systematic medicine.

records.title: Regional organization of nutrient absorption across the small intestine
records.description: The mammalian small intestine is spatially segregated across its length according to distinct processes and functions, including nutrient absorption and protection against environmental insults such as pathogens. This Review examines the regional organization of the small-intestinal epithelium, highlighting molecular, cellular and functional features during development and disease.

records.title: Engineering immune cell therapies for inflammatory bowel disease: from stem cells to CAR T cells
records.description: In this Perspective, Neurath and colleagues discuss immune cell therapies for inflammatory bowel disease, including stem cell-based approaches, regulatory T cell therapies and chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapies. They also discuss future directions for research.

records.title: Actin cytoskeletal dynamics in hepatic myofibroblasts and fibrosis
records.description: Liver fibrosis drives chronic liver disease and liver cancer. This Review dissects how actin cytoskeleton dynamics and related pathways govern hepatic stellate activation and fibrogenesis with implications for targeted therapy.

records.title: Synthetic data generation: challenges and perspectives for gastrointestinal medicine
records.description: The advent of artificial intelligence modalities signifies new advances in medical practice. This Perspective discusses synthetic data generation in the context of gastrointestinal medicine and provides insights into challenges and limitations.

records.title: Steatotic liver disease in Latin America: current views and perspectives
records.description: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) burden is rising worldwide, and Latin America is disproportionately affected. This Review provides a detailed summary of SLD epidemiology in the region, identifies gaps in clinical management and research, and provides suggestions to improve health outcomes.

records.title: Positive results for daraxonrasib for previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer
Dietary perturbation and microbial adaptation in the gut
European Congress on Obesity 2026
A people-first, systems-oriented approach to liver disease in HIV infection
Identifying MASLD patient eligibility for pharmacological therapy: the need to integrate evidence into clinical practice
records.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is a leading cause of chronic liver disease, with rising liver transplantation rates. New therapies such as resmetirom and semaglutide mark a shift in treatment. However, identifying suitable patients remains challenging, requiring integrated approaches combining fibrosis stage, metabolic factors and non-invasive tools in real-world practice.

records.title: Digestive Disease Week 2026
Sequencing what we eat
records.description: Dietary assessment commonly relies on asking people what they remember eating. Genomic methods can change this assessment, paralleling how DNA sequencing revolutionized microbiology. By identifying consumed foods directly from stool, these approaches offer an objective, scalable alternative that gastroenterology researchers can begin using today.

records.title: Precision nutrition for the prevention and management of inflammatory bowel disease
records.description: Diet and nutrition have emerged as promising approaches for the prevention and management of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). This Review outlines a stepwise framework for precision nutrition for IBD, highlighting how dietary recommendations can be tailored to the individual based on a range of characteristics (including demographics and multiomics data) and key considerations for clinical translation.

records.title: Understanding development and cellular plasticity in the pancreas in health and disease
records.description: Pancreatic development is a dynamic process. This Review discusses the development and cellular plasticity that occurs in the pancreas in health and disease, with insights into early development, endocrine and exocrine lineages and the pancreatic microenvironment.

records.title: Cirrhosis, portal hypertension and hepatocellular carcinoma: a stage-based approach
records.description: Cirrhosis, portal hypertension and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are interconnected but are often addressed separately. This Review outlines the key interactions between portal hypertension and HCC in cirrhosis, and explores the management of these conditions across all stages, proposing an integrated, stage-based management framework.

records.title: Human deskilling in medical artificial intelligence: prohibited or permissible under the EU Artificial Intelligence Act?
records.description: Artificial intelligence is rapidly being adopted in healthcare, but studies have shown a ‘deskilling’ phenomenon. Routine exposure to medical artificial intelligence can pose deskilling risks for physicians. We discuss these risks and whether such systems violate the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, the world’s first comprehensive regulatory framework on artificial intelligence.

records.title: Liver disease care amid wars and conflicts
records.description: This Comment highlights the effects of war- and armed conflict-related healthcare disruptions on chronic liver conditions — a crisis that increases morbidity and mortality. Major disruption mechanisms are described, and we advocate for conflict-adapted hepatology guidelines and practical, multi-level response strategies appropriate for armed conflict-associated humanitarian situations.

records.title: γδ T cells in colorectal and liver cancer
records.description: γδ T cells are an important component of local immune surveillance. This Review discusses their role in colorectal cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma development and provides a detailed overview of their therapeutic potential.

records.title: The critical role of gut–brain signalling in eating behaviour and obesity
records.description: This Review outlines the role of gut–brain signalling in eating behaviour and obesity, highlighting gut-derived signals and cues relevant during eating phases. Underlying mechanisms of this gut–brain communication are discussed alongside the key role of the vagus nerve in this process.

records.title: Deciphering cytochrome P450 reductase role in MASLD: molecular mechanisms and pathophysiological implications
records.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves multifactorial metabolic, inflammatory and oxidative stress-driven pathology. In this Perspective, we highlight the role of cytochrome P450 oxidoreductase (CPR) as a potentially overlooked regulator of pathways shaping MASLD development and progression.

records.title: What do we mean by gut health?
records.description: A new Consensus Statement puts forward a definition of ‘gut health’ in an attempt to bring some clarity and consistency to a term that is widely used but often ill-defined and vague.

records.title: Global position statement supporting a World Health Assembly resolution on steatotic liver disease
records.description: Steatotic liver disease has a high human and economic burden, yet remains absent from WHO normative guidance, action plans and strategies. This position statement — endorsed by patient, national and international organizations from around the world — calls on the World Health Assembly to pass the first ever steatotic liver disease resolution.

records.title: Lifespan approaches for the prevention and management of steatotic liver disease
records.description: Steatotic liver disease (SLD), including metabolic dysfunction-associated SLD, requires an age-tailored treatment approach across the life course. This Review highlights age-adjusted lifestyle approaches (such as diet and physical activity) for the prevention and management of SLD, with insights and practical guidance across age groups, from infancy to older age.

records.title: Autoimmune gastritis: emerging insights and clinical management
records.description: In this Review, Lenti and colleagues discuss advances in the epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical management and endoscopic surveillance of autoimmune gastritis. They also outline directions for future research.

records.title: Engineered oesophagus transplantation in a pig model
Liquid biopsy combined with machine learning predicts early detection in liver disease
Gut microbiota induce browning of white adipose tissue
Diet–microbiome associations
Beyond class effects: moving towards drug-level precision in inflammatory bowel disease therapy
records.description: Drug classes offer convenient clinical shorthand but obscure meaningful differences between individual therapies in inflammatory bowel disease. As treatment options expand, moving beyond class effects towards drug-level selection informed by pharmacology, efficacy, safety and patient context is essential to deliver more precise care.

records.title: Microplastics, nanoplastics and liver disease: an emerging health concern?
records.description: Concerns have been raised as to whether microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs) influence human health. This Perspective examines the emerging evidence on MNP accumulation in the liver and its potential effects on human liver health and disease. Research gaps and priorities are also addressed.

records.title: The microbiome regulates host metabolic health and diseases through microbial enzymes
records.description: In this Review, Jiang and colleagues describe how gut microbial enzymes regulate host metabolic health and diseases. They also discuss the methodology for studying gut microbial enzymes and their potential clinical applications.

records.title: Pathophysiology of colitis-associated colorectal cancer
records.description: In this Review, Neufert and Neurath discuss the pathophysiological mechanisms of colitis-associated colorectal cancer, focusing on the tumour epithelium, stromal cells, mucosal barrier and mechanisms of tumour development. They also discuss potential implications for personalized therapy.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in inflammatory bowel disease: bridging innovation, implementation and impact
records.description: In this Perspective, Iacucci and colleagues describe the role of artificial intelligence in inflammatory bowel disease care, highlighting emerging applications as well as implications for implementation.

records.title: Therapeutic targets for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis: a personalized approach to disease management
records.description: Current drug approvals reshape metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) therapeutic strategies. This Review highlights current and emerging therapeutic targets and discusses a mechanism-based framework for personalized, combination-oriented management in MASH.

records.title: Defining ‘gut health’: a leap forward, but still some road to travel
records.description: ‘Gut health’ is a widely used term, but there is much uncertainty and inconsistency related to its use. An international panel has now provided a definition that includes consideration of both gastrointestinal function and symptom burden. While advancing the field, the definition also prompts a number of areas of debate.

records.title: Research without borders: advancing equitable global partnerships to accelerate HBV elimination efforts
records.description: The elimination of hepatitis B will not be achieved through innovation alone. It requires dismantling the structural inequities that have long constrained who leads, funds and benefits from global hepatitis B research.

records.title: Physical activity and the gut
ECCO’26
Long-term data for ileocaecal resection for ileal Crohn’s disease
HIV-associated gut microbiome influences gut mucosal immunity
Microplastics and nanoplastics in the human gut: from signals to standards
records.description: The gastrointestinal tract is a critical interface for microplastic and nanoplastic exposure, yet causal links to health outcomes remain uncertain. We outline current methodological challenges and provide a list of minimum standards for rigorous study design, standardized reporting and careful attention to interpretations to distinguish mechanism from signals.

records.title: Metabotherapy for intestinal disease: using metabolites to prevent and treat disorders of the gut
records.description: Metabolites are important mediators of metabolism at the cellular and organismal levels. This Review explores the concept of metabotherapy, harnessing metabolites to prevent and treat gastrointestinal disorders, providing insights into metabolite classifications and their pathophysiological mechanisms in health and disease and mapping their potential as therapeutic targets.

records.title: Hepatitis C elimination: is it time to redefine the goals?
records.description: Direct-acting antiviral agents have substantially improved the rate of sustained virologic response and safety in the treatment of hepatitis C. However, concerns about the long-term outcomes for individuals who achieve sustained virologic response still exist. Herein, we propose a new conceptual model for redefining the goals and strategies of ongoing hepatitis C elimination campaigns.

records.title: The ethics of unlicensed therapy use in primary biliary cholangitis: a counter view
Reply to ‘The ethics of unlicensed therapy use in primary biliary cholangitis: a counter view’
The International Scientific Association for Probiotics and Prebiotics (ISAPP) consensus statement on the definition and scope of gut health
records.description: This Consensus Statement provides a definition of the term ‘gut health’, as well as a discussion of the relevant domains that contribute to gut health and a framework for appropriate use of the term in the context of therapeutic interventions.

records.title: Germline mutations and somatic mosaicism in steatotic liver diseases and related liver carcinogenesis
records.description: Steatotic liver diseases affect millions worldwide through alcohol and metabolic insults. This Review highlights steatotic liver disease genetic architecture, how it informs disease biology, drug discovery and risk stratification through polygenic risk scores and the need for improved clinical applications.

records.title: ENPP1 as a contributor to chronic pancreatitis-related PDAC
Nutritional maintenance therapy for paediatric patients with Crohn’s disease
In vivo-generated anti-FAP CAR T cells reduced fibrosis in MASH mice
Hepatic recompensation in patients with alcohol-related cirrhosis after alcohol cessation
Lessons learned from viral hepatitis testing that inform law and policy responses to steatotic liver disease
records.description: Steatotic liver disease (SLD), which might lead to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, is on the rise worldwide. This Expert Recommendation draws on lessons learned to tackle viral hepatitis and proposes a framework for SLD screening and testing policies.

records.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and steatohepatitis-associated hepatocarcinoma preclinical models
records.description: Preclinical models are essential to study disease pathogenesis and test novel treatments. Here, a broad overview of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and steatohepatitis-associated hepatocarcinoma preclinical models is provided, detailing main features, advances and limitations of in vitro and in vivo models, and how they translate to human disease.

records.title: Dietary guidelines for gastrointestinal disorders: key to optimizing practice but more work needed
records.description: Nutrition and dietary guidelines in gastrointestinal disorders vary in scope, rigour and recommendations, contributing to variations in practice. This Comment identifies nutrition and dietary guidelines for gastrointestinal disorders, namely chronic constipation, irritable bowel syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease, and examines the methodologies used to develop them.

records.title: The fate of dietary protein in the gastrointestinal tract and implications for colonic disease
records.description: Protein is an essential nutrient in the human diet. This Review explores the fate of dietary protein in the gastrointestinal tract and its influence on colonic health and disease, providing insights into dietary protein metabolism, digestion, absorption, fermentation and the implications for colonic health.

records.title: Pancreatic cancer: advances in immunology, translational analyses and therapeutic paradigms
records.description: Some of the highlights in the pancreatic cancer field in 2025 include long-term data on personalized neoantigen vaccine approaches in resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma, detailed clinico-genomic analyses of large clinical trial datasets, and therapeutic strategies for early-stage disease.

records.title: Drug approvals in 2025 in gastroenterology and hepatology
Balancing cholesterol metabolism in the liver and gut: perspectives in health and disease
records.description: In this Review, Brown and colleagues describe the latest insights into the role of cholesterol synthesis and metabolism in the gut and liver, and implications in diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, hepatocellular carcinoma and colorectal cancer.

records.title: Preventive hepatology for MASLD in the MENA region: reframing care from late-stage treatment to early intervention
records.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most common chronic liver disease worldwide, with the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) being severely affected. By shifting towards preventive hepatology, MENA can mitigate the rising tide of MASLD and its complications, reduce health system costs and improve patient outcomes.

records.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical management
records.description: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) is a complex syndrome characterized by acute hepatic decompensation superimposed on pre-existing chronic liver disease or cirrhosis. This Review provides an update on definitions, pathophysiological mechanisms, clinical presentation and management of ACLF.

records.title: Author Correction: Μetabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a condition of heterogeneous metabolic risk factors, mechanisms and comorbidities requiring holistic treatment
Mucosal glycans: key drivers of the development of inflammatory bowel disease and a potential new therapeutic target
records.description: Glycans are essential components of the gut mucosa that modulate epithelial barrier integrity, host–microbiota interactions and gut immune response. This Review discusses the role of mucosal glycans in gut homeostasis, in intestinal inflammation and their therapeutic potential for inflammatory bowel disease.

records.title: Epigenetics in inflammatory bowel disease: from mechanistic insights to personalized therapeutic strategies
records.description: This Review discusses the complex role of epigenetics in inflammatory bowel disease and provides a comprehensive overview of current and emerging technologies that could enhance the prognostic value of epigenetic biomarkers.

As a new generation of Chinese investigators emerges around the globe, initiatives that foster international collaboration, mentorship and scientific exchange will be essential for advancing the future of global liver research.

records.title: The microbial mirror: how a disrupted microbiome forecasts disease and why policy must act
records.description: Noncommunicable diseases kill 43 million people worldwide yearly, but one of their key biological drivers, the disruption of the gut microbiome by modifiable environmental factors, is still underappreciated by health stakeholders. The translation of microbiome science into concrete actions, from food safety regulators to public health authorities and policymakers, is urgently needed.

records.title: Phase I trial of faecal microbiome transplantation for food allergy
Sexual dimorphism in the liver
records.description: In this Review, Jain and Monga describe the mechanisms of hepatic sexual dimorphism in homeostasis and physiological conditions, as well as in the pathophysiology of diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, autoimmune diseases, viral hepatitis and liver cancer.

records.title: Relieving IBD with duvakitug
Noninvasive testing for fibrosis and cirrhosis in MASLD
From researcher to CEO: closing the gap between discovery and delivery
records.description: A patient advocate asked what decades of fibrosis research meant for the people he represented. I had no answer. That question exposed a gap that the scientific community must now confront: between the knowledge we generate and the means to deliver it to patients.

records.title: Global epidemiology of metabolic and alcohol-associated liver disease: risk factors, natural history and clinical implications
records.description: In this Review, Loomba and colleagues describe the global epidemiology, risk factors, natural history and clinical implications of metabolic and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD).

records.title: Viral pyroptosis linked to lethal hepatic lipid accumulation
Author Correction: The dynamic spectrum of steatotic liver disease: the global perspective
The dynamic spectrum of steatotic liver disease: the global perspective
records.description: Steatotic liver disease encompasses a spectrum of conditions driven by metabolic dysfunction and/or alcohol consumption. This Review provides a comprehensive global overview of the disease and critically examines current therapeutic strategies and future perspectives.

records.title: Multidisciplinary Delphi consensus statement on minimal standards for clinical metadata and end points in microbiome studies
records.description: In this Consensus Statement, an international panel of experts provides recommendations to harmonize metadata, sampling, analysis and end points in gut microbiome-based clinical research.

records.title: Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections
records.description: Anorectal bacterial sexually transmitted infections (STIs) remain a global health challenge. This Review provides an overview of anorectal bacterial STIs focusing on chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis, with insights into global burden, pathophysiology, management and prevention, as well as highlighting knowledge gaps and research priorities.

records.title: Desynchronization of intestinal circadian clocks and gastrointestinal dysfunction
records.description: Intestinal circadian clocks are emerging as important regulators of gastrointestinal physiology and homeostasis. Recent advances suggest that desynchronization of circadian clocks in distinct intestinal cell types could contribute to gastrointestinal dysfunction, highlighting new opportunities to understand disease mechanisms and identify future research priorities.

records.title: Understanding intrapancreatic fat: charting a path forward
records.description: Two independent Delphi-driven consensus initiatives have established the first standardized frameworks for defining, measuring and managing intrapancreatic fat. Their areas of agreement provide a foundation for clinical recognition, while key divergences in terminology, thresholds and evidence appraisal highlight critical questions that must be resolved through rigorous collaborative research.

records.title: Dupilumab shows promise in eosinophilic gastritis
Precision adherence support for hepatitis C treatment
PIEZO1 senses the mechanics of liver regeneration
Steatosis fuels replacement liver metastases in colorectal cancer
Conceptual framework and expert guidance on intrapancreatic fat deposition: the Melbourne consensus
records.description: In this Consensus Statement, a global multidisciplinary group of experts provide a structured framework and clear guidance on intrapancreatic fat deposition and fatty pancreas disorder.

records.title: Features of immune microenvironment associated with colorectal polyp development
Mechanisms and clinical outcomes linking HLA-DRB1*01:03 and IBD
EASL Congress 2026
Advancing liver health in a shifting global landscape
records.description: Global liver health is at a pivotal moment, marked by a rising steatotic liver disease burden alongside stalled progress in viral hepatitis elimination. Strengthening prevention and access to care is essential to reduce inequities, morbidity and mortality worldwide.

records.title: The mesenteric model of abdominal anatomy
records.description: The mesenteric model is a new anatomy of the abdomen that defines a mesentery-based organ system unifying structure, development and function, reveals system-level mechanisms of disease, enables targeted therapies, and provides a coherent scientific foundation for integrating biological research with clinical practice across both abdominal and systematic medicine.

records.title: Regional organization of nutrient absorption across the small intestine
records.description: The mammalian small intestine is spatially segregated across its length according to distinct processes and functions, including nutrient absorption and protection against environmental insults such as pathogens. This Review examines the regional organization of the small-intestinal epithelium, highlighting molecular, cellular and functional features during development and disease.

records.title: Engineering immune cell therapies for inflammatory bowel disease: from stem cells to CAR T cells
records.description: In this Perspective, Neurath and colleagues discuss immune cell therapies for inflammatory bowel disease, including stem cell-based approaches, regulatory T cell therapies and chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapies. They also discuss future directions for research.

records.title: Actin cytoskeletal dynamics in hepatic myofibroblasts and fibrosis
records.description: Liver fibrosis drives chronic liver disease and liver cancer. This Review dissects how actin cytoskeleton dynamics and related pathways govern hepatic stellate activation and fibrogenesis with implications for targeted therapy.

records.title: Synthetic data generation: challenges and perspectives for gastrointestinal medicine
records.description: The advent of artificial intelligence modalities signifies new advances in medical practice. This Perspective discusses synthetic data generation in the context of gastrointestinal medicine and provides insights into challenges and limitations.

records.title: Steatotic liver disease in Latin America: current views and perspectives
records.description: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) burden is rising worldwide, and Latin America is disproportionately affected. This Review provides a detailed summary of SLD epidemiology in the region, identifies gaps in clinical management and research, and provides suggestions to improve health outcomes.

records.title: Positive results for daraxonrasib for previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer
Dietary perturbation and microbial adaptation in the gut
European Congress on Obesity 2026
A people-first, systems-oriented approach to liver disease in HIV infection
Identifying MASLD patient eligibility for pharmacological therapy: the need to integrate evidence into clinical practice
records.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is a leading cause of chronic liver disease, with rising liver transplantation rates. New therapies such as resmetirom and semaglutide mark a shift in treatment. However, identifying suitable patients remains challenging, requiring integrated approaches combining fibrosis stage, metabolic factors and non-invasive tools in real-world practice.

records.title: Digestive Disease Week 2026
Sequencing what we eat
records.description: Dietary assessment commonly relies on asking people what they remember eating. Genomic methods can change this assessment, paralleling how DNA sequencing revolutionized microbiology. By identifying consumed foods directly from stool, these approaches offer an objective, scalable alternative that gastroenterology researchers can begin using today.

records.title: Precision nutrition for the prevention and management of inflammatory bowel disease
records.description: Diet and nutrition have emerged as promising approaches for the prevention and management of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). This Review outlines a stepwise framework for precision nutrition for IBD, highlighting how dietary recommendations can be tailored to the individual based on a range of characteristics (including demographics and multiomics data) and key considerations for clinical translation.

records.title: Understanding development and cellular plasticity in the pancreas in health and disease
records.description: Pancreatic development is a dynamic process. This Review discusses the development and cellular plasticity that occurs in the pancreas in health and disease, with insights into early development, endocrine and exocrine lineages and the pancreatic microenvironment.

records.title: Cirrhosis, portal hypertension and hepatocellular carcinoma: a stage-based approach
records.description: Cirrhosis, portal hypertension and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are interconnected but are often addressed separately. This Review outlines the key interactions between portal hypertension and HCC in cirrhosis, and explores the management of these conditions across all stages, proposing an integrated, stage-based management framework.

records.title: Human deskilling in medical artificial intelligence: prohibited or permissible under the EU Artificial Intelligence Act?
records.description: Artificial intelligence is rapidly being adopted in healthcare, but studies have shown a ‘deskilling’ phenomenon. Routine exposure to medical artificial intelligence can pose deskilling risks for physicians. We discuss these risks and whether such systems violate the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, the world’s first comprehensive regulatory framework on artificial intelligence.

records.title: Liver disease care amid wars and conflicts
records.description: This Comment highlights the effects of war- and armed conflict-related healthcare disruptions on chronic liver conditions — a crisis that increases morbidity and mortality. Major disruption mechanisms are described, and we advocate for conflict-adapted hepatology guidelines and practical, multi-level response strategies appropriate for armed conflict-associated humanitarian situations.

records.title: γδ T cells in colorectal and liver cancer
records.description: γδ T cells are an important component of local immune surveillance. This Review discusses their role in colorectal cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma development and provides a detailed overview of their therapeutic potential.

records.title: The critical role of gut–brain signalling in eating behaviour and obesity
records.description: This Review outlines the role of gut–brain signalling in eating behaviour and obesity, highlighting gut-derived signals and cues relevant during eating phases. Underlying mechanisms of this gut–brain communication are discussed alongside the key role of the vagus nerve in this process.

records.title: Deciphering cytochrome P450 reductase role in MASLD: molecular mechanisms and pathophysiological implications
records.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves multifactorial metabolic, inflammatory and oxidative stress-driven pathology. In this Perspective, we highlight the role of cytochrome P450 oxidoreductase (CPR) as a potentially overlooked regulator of pathways shaping MASLD development and progression.

records.title: What do we mean by gut health?
records.description: A new Consensus Statement puts forward a definition of ‘gut health’ in an attempt to bring some clarity and consistency to a term that is widely used but often ill-defined and vague.

records.title: Global position statement supporting a World Health Assembly resolution on steatotic liver disease
records.description: Steatotic liver disease has a high human and economic burden, yet remains absent from WHO normative guidance, action plans and strategies. This position statement — endorsed by patient, national and international organizations from around the world — calls on the World Health Assembly to pass the first ever steatotic liver disease resolution.

records.title: Lifespan approaches for the prevention and management of steatotic liver disease
records.description: Steatotic liver disease (SLD), including metabolic dysfunction-associated SLD, requires an age-tailored treatment approach across the life course. This Review highlights age-adjusted lifestyle approaches (such as diet and physical activity) for the prevention and management of SLD, with insights and practical guidance across age groups, from infancy to older age.

records.title: Autoimmune gastritis: emerging insights and clinical management
records.description: In this Review, Lenti and colleagues discuss advances in the epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical management and endoscopic surveillance of autoimmune gastritis. They also outline directions for future research.

records.title: Engineered oesophagus transplantation in a pig model
Liquid biopsy combined with machine learning predicts early detection in liver disease
Gut microbiota induce browning of white adipose tissue
Diet–microbiome associations
Beyond class effects: moving towards drug-level precision in inflammatory bowel disease therapy
records.description: Drug classes offer convenient clinical shorthand but obscure meaningful differences between individual therapies in inflammatory bowel disease. As treatment options expand, moving beyond class effects towards drug-level selection informed by pharmacology, efficacy, safety and patient context is essential to deliver more precise care.

records.title: Microplastics, nanoplastics and liver disease: an emerging health concern?
records.description: Concerns have been raised as to whether microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs) influence human health. This Perspective examines the emerging evidence on MNP accumulation in the liver and its potential effects on human liver health and disease. Research gaps and priorities are also addressed.

records.title: The microbiome regulates host metabolic health and diseases through microbial enzymes
records.description: In this Review, Jiang and colleagues describe how gut microbial enzymes regulate host metabolic health and diseases. They also discuss the methodology for studying gut microbial enzymes and their potential clinical applications.

records.title: Pathophysiology of colitis-associated colorectal cancer
records.description: In this Review, Neufert and Neurath discuss the pathophysiological mechanisms of colitis-associated colorectal cancer, focusing on the tumour epithelium, stromal cells, mucosal barrier and mechanisms of tumour development. They also discuss potential implications for personalized therapy.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in inflammatory bowel disease: bridging innovation, implementation and impact
records.description: In this Perspective, Iacucci and colleagues describe the role of artificial intelligence in inflammatory bowel disease care, highlighting emerging applications as well as implications for implementation.

records.title: Therapeutic targets for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis: a personalized approach to disease management
records.description: Current drug approvals reshape metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) therapeutic strategies. This Review highlights current and emerging therapeutic targets and discusses a mechanism-based framework for personalized, combination-oriented management in MASH.

records.title: Defining ‘gut health’: a leap forward, but still some road to travel
records.description: ‘Gut health’ is a widely used term, but there is much uncertainty and inconsistency related to its use. An international panel has now provided a definition that includes consideration of both gastrointestinal function and symptom burden. While advancing the field, the definition also prompts a number of areas of debate.

records.title: Research without borders: advancing equitable global partnerships to accelerate HBV elimination efforts
records.description: The elimination of hepatitis B will not be achieved through innovation alone. It requires dismantling the structural inequities that have long constrained who leads, funds and benefits from global hepatitis B research.

records.title: Physical activity and the gut
ECCO’26
Long-term data for ileocaecal resection for ileal Crohn’s disease
HIV-associated gut microbiome influences gut mucosal immunity
Microplastics and nanoplastics in the human gut: from signals to standards
records.description: The gastrointestinal tract is a critical interface for microplastic and nanoplastic exposure, yet causal links to health outcomes remain uncertain. We outline current methodological challenges and provide a list of minimum standards for rigorous study design, standardized reporting and careful attention to interpretations to distinguish mechanism from signals.

records.title: Metabotherapy for intestinal disease: using metabolites to prevent and treat disorders of the gut
records.description: Metabolites are important mediators of metabolism at the cellular and organismal levels. This Review explores the concept of metabotherapy, harnessing metabolites to prevent and treat gastrointestinal disorders, providing insights into metabolite classifications and their pathophysiological mechanisms in health and disease and mapping their potential as therapeutic targets.

records.title: Hepatitis C elimination: is it time to redefine the goals?
records.description: Direct-acting antiviral agents have substantially improved the rate of sustained virologic response and safety in the treatment of hepatitis C. However, concerns about the long-term outcomes for individuals who achieve sustained virologic response still exist. Herein, we propose a new conceptual model for redefining the goals and strategies of ongoing hepatitis C elimination campaigns.

records.title: The ethics of unlicensed therapy use in primary biliary cholangitis: a counter view
Reply to ‘The ethics of unlicensed therapy use in primary biliary cholangitis: a counter view’
The International Scientific Association for Probiotics and Prebiotics (ISAPP) consensus statement on the definition and scope of gut health
records.description: This Consensus Statement provides a definition of the term ‘gut health’, as well as a discussion of the relevant domains that contribute to gut health and a framework for appropriate use of the term in the context of therapeutic interventions.

records.title: Germline mutations and somatic mosaicism in steatotic liver diseases and related liver carcinogenesis
records.description: Steatotic liver diseases affect millions worldwide through alcohol and metabolic insults. This Review highlights steatotic liver disease genetic architecture, how it informs disease biology, drug discovery and risk stratification through polygenic risk scores and the need for improved clinical applications.

records.title: ENPP1 as a contributor to chronic pancreatitis-related PDAC
Nutritional maintenance therapy for paediatric patients with Crohn’s disease
In vivo-generated anti-FAP CAR T cells reduced fibrosis in MASH mice
Hepatic recompensation in patients with alcohol-related cirrhosis after alcohol cessation
Lessons learned from viral hepatitis testing that inform law and policy responses to steatotic liver disease
records.description: Steatotic liver disease (SLD), which might lead to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, is on the rise worldwide. This Expert Recommendation draws on lessons learned to tackle viral hepatitis and proposes a framework for SLD screening and testing policies.

records.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and steatohepatitis-associated hepatocarcinoma preclinical models
records.description: Preclinical models are essential to study disease pathogenesis and test novel treatments. Here, a broad overview of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and steatohepatitis-associated hepatocarcinoma preclinical models is provided, detailing main features, advances and limitations of in vitro and in vivo models, and how they translate to human disease.

records.title: Dietary guidelines for gastrointestinal disorders: key to optimizing practice but more work needed
records.description: Nutrition and dietary guidelines in gastrointestinal disorders vary in scope, rigour and recommendations, contributing to variations in practice. This Comment identifies nutrition and dietary guidelines for gastrointestinal disorders, namely chronic constipation, irritable bowel syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease, and examines the methodologies used to develop them.

records.title: The fate of dietary protein in the gastrointestinal tract and implications for colonic disease
records.description: Protein is an essential nutrient in the human diet. This Review explores the fate of dietary protein in the gastrointestinal tract and its influence on colonic health and disease, providing insights into dietary protein metabolism, digestion, absorption, fermentation and the implications for colonic health.

records.title: Pancreatic cancer: advances in immunology, translational analyses and therapeutic paradigms
records.description: Some of the highlights in the pancreatic cancer field in 2025 include long-term data on personalized neoantigen vaccine approaches in resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma, detailed clinico-genomic analyses of large clinical trial datasets, and therapeutic strategies for early-stage disease.

records.title: Drug approvals in 2025 in gastroenterology and hepatology
Balancing cholesterol metabolism in the liver and gut: perspectives in health and disease
records.description: In this Review, Brown and colleagues describe the latest insights into the role of cholesterol synthesis and metabolism in the gut and liver, and implications in diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, hepatocellular carcinoma and colorectal cancer.

records.title: Preventive hepatology for MASLD in the MENA region: reframing care from late-stage treatment to early intervention
records.description: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most common chronic liver disease worldwide, with the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) being severely affected. By shifting towards preventive hepatology, MENA can mitigate the rising tide of MASLD and its complications, reduce health system costs and improve patient outcomes.

records.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical management
records.description: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) is a complex syndrome characterized by acute hepatic decompensation superimposed on pre-existing chronic liver disease or cirrhosis. This Review provides an update on definitions, pathophysiological mechanisms, clinical presentation and management of ACLF.

records.title: Author Correction: Μetabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a condition of heterogeneous metabolic risk factors, mechanisms and comorbidities requiring holistic treatment
Mucosal glycans: key drivers of the development of inflammatory bowel disease and a potential new therapeutic target
records.description: Glycans are essential components of the gut mucosa that modulate epithelial barrier integrity, host–microbiota interactions and gut immune response. This Review discusses the role of mucosal glycans in gut homeostasis, in intestinal inflammation and their therapeutic potential for inflammatory bowel disease.
